description: US-32 One household at a time at the counter. TWO CHANGES TO /ausgabe, both from DF after they worked real afternoons on it, and one batch because they are one screen and largely one set of files. A — THE WALK IS WITHDRAWN. Zurück/Weiter (US-21) step through today's group in customer-number order, and DF do not call households that way: they call them in BLOCKS — "everyone from 1 to 30 now" — and within a block households arrive in whatever order they turn up, so the person at the counter is almost never the next number. The buttons were not wrong; the assumption behind them was. US-21 is withdrawn the way US-22 withdrew the week-colour lookup, and the documents that asked for it are part of the change rather than an afterthought. B — A RECORDED HAND-OUT CLEARS THE SCREEN. Everything on screen about a served household is finished business, and the next person is already at the counter — so today the screen shows one household while another stands in front of it. After the write the screen returns to its INITIAL STATE (banner, group progress, empty focused number field) and a CONFIRMATION AT THE TOP names the customer number, the name, the amount taken and the time, with a „Korrigieren" link one click back to them. It stands until the NEXT LOOKUP and no longer — no timer, no dismiss control — and the group tally, one higher, is the standing evidence the hand-out landed. WHAT MUST NOT BE CLEARED: only a SUCCESSFULLY RECORDED hand-out clears the screen. A refusal, and the question an amount above the amount asked for raises, leave the household and the question standing — nothing may be cleared while an answer is owed. A SAVED CORRECTION does not clear either: the staff member is working on that record. Removing a hand-out and archiving keep the returns they already have. R-15 CORRECTED ON A POINT OF FACT: the source document says an already-served household is shown as a red refusal. It is not — evaluateAtCounter takes no record, so lookupCustomer answers CLEAR_TO_SERVE and the screen shows the GREEN „Ausgabe frei" banner, while the ALREADY_SERVED_TODAY verdict sits in the union unreachable. Green is the worse of the two mistakes, and looking a served household up again is now the ORDINARY route to a correction, so stories 4–6 make that verdict reachable and state it as a fact in muted chrome — never red, and never offering a second hand-out. NO SCHEMA CHANGE, NO MIGRATION, NO NEW PORT METHOD and no infrastructure file: every fact this batch needs is already loaded by lookupCustomer and readGroupRoster. BUILD ORDER: requirement A is a DELETION and runs OUTSIDE-IN (screen → use case → domain), the inverse of every other batch; requirement B is additive and runs inside-out. THE TWO TRAPS, both silent: recordAttendance evaluates the verdict BEFORE canRecord, so a verdict that knows the day's record turns a duplicate hand-out into NotClearToServe and rewords the counter's refusal — the canRecord check moves above it (story 5); and CertificateControls derives its expired prop from the verdict KIND, so a served household would lose its reminder controls on re-lookup once ALREADY_SERVED_TODAY outranks CLEAR_TO_SERVE_CERTIFICATE_EXPIRED — the prop moves onto a certificateExpired field on the lookup view (stories 5 and 6). Neither would fail an existing test. Source PRD: tasks/prd-us-32-one-household-at-a-time.md; DF's own words in local_only/ausgabe_screen/refined-requirements.md.
